title: Plot structure
examples: How do I know where the climax is in a story?
Can you show me an example of exposition?
What is the difference between falling action and resolution?

explain.say: Today we are learning about plot structure in stories.

items: Exposition: Introduction of characters and setting
Rising Action: Building tension and conflict
Climax: The most exciting turning point
Falling Action: Events after the peak
Resolution: The conclusion where things settle

explain.say: The exposition sets the scene and introduces the main characters. This is where the story begins for you.
The rising action builds the conflict and makes things more intense. The problems start to grow bigger here.
The climax is the turning point; it is the moment of highest tension. Something big happens right here.
After the climax, the falling action shows the immediate results. The story starts to calm down a little bit.
The resolution wraps up all the loose ends and shows the new normal. The story feels complete for you.

items: The conflict is solved | Loose ends are tied | Story concludes

faq.q: What is the difference between the climax and the resolution?
faq.a: The climax is the moment of greatest action or tension in the story. The resolution is what happens after the climax, where everything settles down.
asks: What happens after the big fight?

faq.q: Does the rising action always lead to a climax?
faq.a: Yes, typically the rising action builds the tension that leads directly into the climax. It is the build-up to the main event.
asks: Is the climax always the biggest thing?

faq.q: Can a story skip the exposition?
faq.a: While some stories start in the middle, the exposition usually provides necessary background information for the reader. It helps us understand the world.
asks: Do I need to know everything at the start?
What if the setting is not clear?

faq.a: It is a model that shows the five main parts of a dramatic plot structure. It helps writers organize their stories effectively.
asks: Is that a type of plot?

faq.a: No, the resolution can be sad, surprising, or even unresolved. It just means the main conflict has reached a final state.
asks: Does it have to be a neat ending?

facts: The exposition introduces the setting and main characters.
The rising action increases the conflict and tension gradually.
The climax is the point of highest emotional or physical tension.
The resolution provides closure to the story's main conflict.

quiz.say: A character faces their biggest challenge during the story's peak moment. This moment is the:
quiz.why: The climax is defined as the point of highest tension.

wrong.0: This is wrong because exposition only sets the scene at the beginning.
wrong.1: This is wrong because resolution is the calming ending, not the peak.
wrong.2: This is wrong because rising action builds up to the peak, it is not the peak itself.

quiz.say: If a story ends by showing the characters living normally after a big event, this is the:
quiz.why: The resolution shows the final state after the conflict has been dealt with.

wrong.0: This is wrong because rising action is about building up, not concluding.
wrong.2: This is wrong because the climax is the action, not the aftermath.
wrong.3: This is wrong because falling action is just the immediate winding down, not the final settling.

quiz.say: The initial part of the story, where we meet the characters and the setting, is called the:
quiz.why: Exposition is the required starting point to introduce the story's world.

wrong.0: This is wrong because the climax is the main event, not the beginning.
wrong.1: This is wrong because resolution is the final wrapping up of the story.
wrong.3: This is wrong because falling action happens much later in the plot.
